item.title: Michigan scientist buried seeds in 1879; some still grew 142 years later in an experiment lasting to 2100
item.description: In a remarkable exploration of seed dormancy, William James Beal's 1879 experiment revealed astonishing results when researchers discovered viable seeds in 2021, 142 years later. This included a surprising hybrid moth mullein detected through DNA analysis, enriching the study's findings. Insights gained will enhance land restoration efforts and help control invasive species for a sustainable future, demonstrating the enduring legacy of scientific inquiry.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: North Carolina father to spend $800,000 building housing community for disabled son and those like him
item.description: Dave Curro is spearheading the development of Forest Grove, an innovative community designed specifically for adults with special needs. This initiative will include 20 tiny homes and a supporting community center, providing essential resources. A recent festival raised significant funds, demonstrating strong community support. Curro's son, Bret, inspires this heartfelt project, addressing a crucial shortage in housing options for this underserved population.

item.title: Old Concrete Powers Upgrade: UDOT recycles 15,000 cubic yards on site; cuts truck trips
item.description: Utah's Bangerter Highway saw old concrete recycled for new road base. Approximately fifteen thousand cubic yards of concrete were crushed on site. This material formed the structural layer beneath new highway interchanges. The recycling process reduced truck journeys and avoided waste disposal. This initiative gave a thirty-year-old highway a significant second life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists use AI to recreate insect calls from Jurassic; some communicated above human hearing
item.description: Scientists have recreated the calls of nine Jurassic insect species that lived 165 million years ago. Using fossilised wings, laser measurements, computer modelling and AI, researchers found that some insects made clear chirping sounds, while one species may have produced ultrasonic calls above the human hearing range.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 33-year-old buys neglected 81-room hotel for $2.55M; is spending $1.1M to rebuild it while living there
item.description: From a modest beginning, Greg Clark has embarked on an impressive journey in the hospitality sector, currently breathing new life into an eighty-one-room hotel located in the picturesque Eureka Springs. His aim is to craft exceptional guest experiences, showcasing his renovation progress on TikTok. With a vision to build ten carefully curated hotels over seven years, Clark's journey is one of ambition and creativity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Devil Flower Species Found: Fungi-fed Thai plant stuns botanists; fewer than 50 exist
item.description: In a remarkable botanical find, scientists have discovered Thismia daemona, a unique flowering plant in Thailand's Thong Pha Phum National Park. This intriguing species, devoid of leaves and green structures, primarily derives its nourishment from subterranean fungi. Its eerie, horn-like form has earned it the moniker 'devil flower' among researchers, marking a significant discovery in the study of this rare plant group.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Trump eyes Pentagon leadership changes as frustration over Iran war grows: Report
item.description: In light of ongoing leadership transitions within the Army, several candidates have emerged as potential successors to the former US Army Secretary. President Trump has been appraised of various options amidst growing tensions from the Iran conflict, though White House and Pentagon sources have refuted rumors regarding a review of the Deputy Secretary of War role. Pressure mounts as frustration escalates over the drawn-out war efforts.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: US warns of rising illnesses in Cuba amid worsening water, power crisis; embassy issues health alert
item.description: The US Embassy in Havana has raised alarms about rising intestinal illnesses in Cuba, attributing them to the deteriorating water and electricity systems on the island. Ongoing restrictions on fuel shipments from the US have intensified these power outages and sanitation issues. Both locals and visitors are advised to exercise caution regarding food safety and refrigeration practices. UN experts caution that these sanctions may exacerbate a larger public health emergency.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: US man duct-taped to seat after attacking passenger mid-flight, racial abuse
item.description: An American Airlines flight traveling from Dallas to Newark had to make an unexpected stop in Baltimore due to a disruptive passenger. The individual reportedly attacked another traveler and directed racial insults toward a flight attendant. Thanks to the quick actions of retired law enforcement officer Juan Mejia and a vigilant flight attendant, the passenger was subdued using zip ties and duct tape for safety.

item.title: Michigan school sold for $40,000 in 2011 now asks $450,000 after one wing became 5 homes
item.description: A former school at Michigan’s K.I. Sawyer Air Force Base has undergone a striking transformation since selling for $40,000 in 2011. The 39,000-square-foot property now features five homes in one renovated wing and is listed for $450,000. Spread across 19.38 acres, the unusual property still includes classrooms, a gym, garages and spaces awaiting renovation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Lilah Mehta, the Connecticut high-school student who entered a Yale lab at 16
item.description: In a groundbreaking achievement, high school student Lilah Mehta has co-authored a significant neuroscience study, diving deep into the world of biological inquiries. Her research, which centered on ion channels potentially related to neurodegenerative diseases, led to a peer-reviewed publication. Overcoming laboratory challenges and grasping complex molecular principles, Mehta has firmly established her passion for both medicine and environmental science.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Donald Trump calls Maria Bartiromo a ‘true warrior’ after Fox News exit, says fans ‘will not be happy’
item.description: Donald Trump has praised Maria Bartiromo as a “true warrior” following her departure from Fox News Media, saying he “can’t believe” she will no longer host her shows. Trump also warned that her many fans “will not be happy.” Bartiromo’s exit comes after more than 12 years with Fox, though her lawyer disputes reports that she was fired.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Joseph Martinek bought a Texas farm in 1911; 115 years later, family protects 470 acres
item.description: Joseph Martinek purchased a Texas farm in 1911, beginning a family legacy that has lasted 115 years. In 2026, his descendants permanently protected 470 acres outside La Grange through a donated conservation easement. The property preserves farmland, wildlife habitat, open space, water resources and archaeological history while allowing the family to retain ownership and continue stewardship.
